subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347 LANDED. FORMAT, rendered from the licensed PDF rather than read from the OCR (scripts/render-spec-page.py, PDF page 734 = printed 704): `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 } ]`, with RELEASE and FROM the underlined required words -- the transcription at 14.9.32.2 is faithful, and the operand IS record-name-1, not identifier-1. THE DIVERGENCE THIS ROW CARRIED (over-acceptance of the record-name-1 POSITION) IS CLOSED: `RELEASE SRT-REC(1:3)` used to compile with NO diagnostic at any --std and emit CobolSort.Release(..., CobolString.RefMod(SRT_REC.AsImage(), 1, 3)), releasing a 3-character record into an 8-byte sort file; it is now COBOL1757 at every edition. The rule behind it: a record-name is a user-defined word (8.3.2.2.25) and 5.2.4's operand table gives that operand type 'User-defined word, including qualification and subscripting if needed' and nothing further, while 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 permits reference modification only 'anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted' -- its NOTE drawing the consequence, 'where data-name-n is used in a general format or syntax rule, then reference-modification is not permitted' (all three --check OK). The refusal is at BIND, not in the grammar: `releaseStatement : RELEASE dataReference` stays general because the subordinate-item half of the same rule cannot be decided by a grammar, and one rule belongs in one place. THE ACCEPTED SURFACE IS UNCHANGED and still verified in both positive goldens: FROM omitted; FROM identifier; FROM subscripted identifier; FROM reference-modified identifier (an IDENTIFIER position, where 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 does permit it); FROM alphanumeric literal; FROM figurative constants (8.3.3.6.3 SR1). EDITION LEG: the literal-1 arm is gated 2002+ (`from-literal-2002` -> COBOL0871, the one FROM-phrase gate WRITE and REWRITE share since kb/Work PB2650); the functionCall arm (the deliberate PB10 addition, legal by 8.4.3.1.2) carries no gate. Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32, so 2014 and 2023 are identical; the 85/2002 boundary of the literal arm is DERIVED, not quoted (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 7.34).
